newsitem.title: FRANCE: ONIC predicts 1997 soft wheat crop of 34.01 mln T. [CORRECTED 11:56 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ONIC predicts 1997 soft wheat crop of 34.01 mln T. [CORRECTED 11:56 GMT]

text.p: France could harvest a 1997 soft wheat crop of 34.01 million tonnes, compared with a record 34.69 million last year, national grain office ONIC predicted on Wednesday.
ONIC's first estimate for the 1997 crop also suggests France could harvest a 1997 barley crop of 9.44 million tonnes, against 9.54 million in 1996.
ONIC expects the durum wheat crop to fall to 933,289 tonnes from 1.25 million last year, and the overall grain crop, excluding maize and sorghum, to drop to 46.07 million tonnes from 47.37 million.
The estimate for the grain crop includes soft and durum wheat, barley, oats, rye, and triticale.

It assumes the average soft wheat yield would fall to 6.92 tonnes per hectare from 7.296 (corrects figure from 7.67) tonnes. But the decline in yields would be partly offset by an 8.66 percent rise in soft wheat sowings to 4.91 million hectares.
The barley yield would decline to 5.83 tonnes from 6.25 tonnes last year, but with sowings up by 6.1 percent to 1.62 million ha.
The durum wheat yield would fall to 3.61 tonnes from 4.65, with sowings down by 4.22 percent to 258,390 hectares.
